messages.subject: texi2dvi does not execute in rapache
messages.subject_clean: texi2dvi does not execute in rapache
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
I'm trying to serve pdfs by using brew+latex on rapache. Inspired by
this post http://biostatmatt.com/archives/1184 which does it by using
sweave instead of brew.

So the idea is that I have a report.brew file which is brew (latex+R
code) file.

The handler picks these brew files and:

1. compiles the brew and creates the tex file
 brew(report.brew, report.tex)

2. compiles the tex file and creates a pdf
texti2dvi(report.tex, pdf=TRUE)

3. redirects the user to the pdf file.

The problem is that while the handler does indeed compile from brew to
tex, the second step: texti2dvi fails.
The error message that shown the browser is:

Error en tools::texi2dvi(texfile, clean = TRUE, pdf = TRUE) :
  Running 'texi2dvi' on '/Library/WebServer/Documents/rreports/
report1.tex' failed.
Traceback:
3: stop(msg, domain = NA)
2: tools::texi2dvi(texfile, clean = TRUE, pdf = TRUE) at
ReportHandler.R#29
1: ReportHandler(file = "/Library/WebServer/Documents/rreports/
report1.brew",
       envir = .rAenv)

the crazy thing is that if i run the handler code in a R console, it
works. texti2dvi does produce the pdf from the brewed tex file.

Here is the hanlder code:

ReportHandler <- function(file, envir) {
  library(brew)
  library(tools)

  oldwd <- getwd()
  setwd(dirname(file))

  # Set up filenames
  #rndname <- paste(sample(letters, 16, replace=TRUE), collapse='')
  bsefile <- paste(sub("\\.[^\\.]*$", "", file))
  texfile <- paste(bsefile, ".tex", sep="")
  pdffile <- paste(bsefile, ".pdf", sep="")
  lnkurl  <- basename(pdffile)

  # brew!
  attach(envir, warn.conflicts=FALSE)
  brew(file, texfile)
  tools::texi2dvi(texfile, clean=TRUE, pdf=TRUE)
  detach(envir)

  # Redirect to the newly created PDF
  setContentType("text/html; charset=UTF-8;")
  cat("<DOCTYPE! html><html><head>")
  cat(paste("<meta http-equiv=\"Refresh\" content=\"0;URL=",
      lnkurl, "\">", sep=""))
  cat("</head><body></body></html>")

  setwd(oldwd)
}

Any idea will be appreciated! :-)

Xavi.

user running the web server cannot create the temporary files
typically produced by a run of latex. Do these two things:

1. Call setwd() to some temporary directory (scope out tempdir() i
think) and then call texi2dvi()
2. Be sure the web server user can create the pdf files where you want them.

Jeff

messages.subject_clean: texi2dvi does not execute in rapache
messages.body_plain:
Hmmm....

I recently had an issue running pdflatex from rApache: temporary fonts
would not be created. I determined this by looking at the .log file
produced by the latex run which pointed to a failed font creation
command. I ended up running the font creation command from a shell
running as the same user as the web server. This fixed the issue in
rApache, but I bet if I created another report that needed a different
font I'd have to do the same shell trick. There may be some
environment variables (possibly $HOME) missing via the web server ->
rApache -> pdflatex execution.

So, try and find the .log file created when rApache runs texi2dvi and
see where that gets you.

messages.subject: Re: Error in dyn.load libpq.so.5 for rApache [ libpq.so.5: cannot open shared object file]
messages.subject_clean: Error in dyn.load libpq.so.5 for rApache [ libpq.so.5: cannot open shared object file]
messages.body_plain:
If you can get RPostgreSQL to work from the command line, do an lsof -p on the R process to see exactly which libpq.so* is being loaded. Scope out your LD_LIBRARY_PATH variable; figure out what's in /etc/ld.so.conf. Once you have that info, then you can troubleshoot rApache to see what's not getting set right. I do understand that some Linux distros like to place apache in a restricted environment upon startup, so CentOS may be doing that as well. I know it's easy to softlink libraries as root to fix these kinds of issues, but that's a rare case. It's always best to follow the distro way. messages.subject: Re: brew+PHP
messages.body_plain:
I recommend you to rethink the problem. What do you actually want to do? <?php /* code */ ?> <%# R code %> can mean lots of stuff.
You can send POST request via PHP cURL module to RApache and use output buffering to grab output from R script, hence put it in your PHP code.

for sending POST requests via PHP, see this link: http://davidwalsh.name/execute-http-post-php-curl
for output buffering, see official manual pages: http://www.php.net/manual/en/book.outcontrol.php

You should do something like this:

<?php

ob_start();
// send POST request with PHP
// R echoes some output
$output = ob_get_clean();
// do stuff with $output

?>

It's advisable to serialize R output to JSON (see RJSONIO package, toJSON() method), and decode it in PHP with json_decode(). But... as you like it...

Note that, in this case, you rarely need to use brew. I don't like the whole idea of using brew to shove R code into HTML/PHP pages. I salute latter approach for dynamic reports in LaTeX, but I tend to evaluate R scripts with sys.source.

Basically, you have your login stuff in the PHP file and then do a "exec" command in PHP to run the R script.   You would output a text file with commands, etc. (that can include variables/data from POST) and then execute R on it.

messages.subject: Re: brew+PHP
messages.body_plain:
I don't like $_SESSION vars, since their safety is quite questionable. But, anyway... you can put your R scripts outside web root, or use .htaccess to prevent direct access to scripts. It's pretty much a standard technique to prevent access to include scripts. http://stackoverflow.com/questions/409496/prevent-direct-access-to-a-php-include-file

By doing so, your R scripts cannot get executed outside PHP scripts. So there...

On Thu, Sep 29, 2011 at 15:02, Christian Parker <c.andre...@gmail.com> wrote:
> It's a password authentication issue. I have some php code that is evaluated at the head of all my pages and redirects if necessary. But now I want my r pages to be protected as well and can't figure out a way to read the session variable in r without posting it for all the world to see. Any ideas?
>
>
>
> On Sep 28, 2011, at 6:44 PM, "Aleksandar Blagotić" <aca.bl...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> > I recommend you to rethink the problem. What do you actually want to do? <?php /* code */ ?> <%# R code %> can mean lots of stuff.
> > You can send POST request via PHP cURL module to RApache and use output buffering to grab output from R script, hence put it in your PHP code.
> >
> > for sending POST requests via PHP, see this link:  <http://davidwalsh.name/execute-http-post-php-curl>http://davidwalsh.name/execute-http-post-php-curl
> > for output buffering, see official manual pages:  <http://www.php.net/manual/en/book.outcontrol.php>http://www.php.net/manual/en/book.outcontrol.php
> >
> > You should do something like this:
> >
> > <?php
> >
> > ob_start();
> > // send POST request with PHP
> > // R echoes some output
> > $output = ob_get_clean();
> > // do stuff with $output
> >
> > ?>
> >
> > It's advisable to serialize R output to JSON (see RJSONIO package, toJSON() method), and decode it in PHP with json_decode(). But... as you like it...
> >
> > Note that, in this case, you rarely need to use brew. I don't like the whole idea of using brew to shove R code into HTML/PHP pages. I salute latter approach for dynamic reports in LaTeX, but I tend to evaluate R scripts with sys.source.
